correctness.rationale: Every feasible star partition has exactly one hub coalition; a leaf with IR preferences never strictly exits it. If the hub is monotone, its first best-response singleton target outranks every currently free singleton and, by monotonicity, every newly freed former hub partner. Hub utility cannot become worse, hence hub changes at most once and all other leaves join at most twice. The additive prize-leaf trace attains \(2n-3\) for all \(n\ge2\). The separately constructed nonmonotone min-index hub has a fully admissible k-stage sequence of k+(k-1)(k-2)/2 best responses on \(n=k+2\) vertices. Under IR, hub utility is nondecreasing across leaf admissions and strictly rises on hub moves, so hub singleton target utilities strictly increase, giving at most n-1 hub moves and quadratic total. Exact finite state-space checks support the analytic arguments.

value.rationale: The 2024 source leaves best-response speed as a scientific question after proving quadratic improvement bounds. The new statement identifies hub monotonicity alone as sufficient for an exact linear maximum, with a local-additive sharpness example, but also exhibits genuinely quadratic best-response paths under individually rational nonmonotone hub preferences. This supplies a natural structural boundary and a counterexample to a blanket speed-up expectation, rather than an arbitrary small-instance count.
